m.title: Improve a weak security answer
m.q: A pupil wrote: 'A firewall makes the Internet safe.' Improve this into a specific two-mark explanation of how a firewall works. [2 marks]
st: The phrase 'makes it safe' is too general to show an exact mechanism.
A firewall checks traffic against configured rules [1].
It blocks disallowed or suspicious connections [1], helping restrict unauthorised network access.
Two linked technical points earn marks; do not claim the firewall stops every attack.

w: An answer says: 'DNS opens the Internet.' Rewrite it as a two-mark explanation of DNS. [2 marks]
DNS looks up an IP address associated with a domain name [1], allowing the client to contact the requested server [1].
An answer says: 'A mesh is better.' Improve it using one advantage and a reason. [2 marks]
Mesh can provide alternative routes [1], so traffic may still get through when a link fails [1].
An answer says: 'Encryption stops hackers.' Write a better two-mark explanation. [2 marks]
Encryption scrambles data into ciphertext [1], so an interceptor without the key cannot readily read it [1].
wSteps: Replace vague wording with the precise DNS job.
DNS resolves a domain to an IP address [1].
The browser uses the IP address to reach the server [1].
DNS looks up an IP address associated with a domain name [1], allowing the client to contact the requested server [1].
Name one topology feature and its impact.
Mesh provides more than one path [1].
Another path may work after a failure [1].

Be specific about data and keys.
Without the key an interceptor cannot interpret content [1].
Encryption scrambles data into ciphertext [1], so an interceptor without the key cannot readily read it [1].
